title: Stocks Recovered From an AI-Fueled Drop To End The Week Despite Higher Oil Prices And Bond Yields
source_used: Yahoo Finance (original URL, read in full)
key_facts: The S&P 500 gained 0.59%, the Nasdaq Composite 0.64% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average 0.83% on Friday 9 Oct 2026, ending the week higher after an AI-led drop on Thursday.

Tech shares rebounded after falling on Thursday on reports that OpenAI's annualized revenue was $50 billion at the end of September, below the $68 billion previously reported (other outlets say about $70 billion).
A further report on Friday said OpenAI expects $70 billion by the end of the year, 40% more than September; the company shared the figure with investors in its fundraising.
OpenAI is seeking at least $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, Bloomberg reported; it raised $122 billion in March at an $852 billion valuation.
University of Michigan consumer sentiment fell to 46.3 in October from 48.1 in September, a five-month low; year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7%.
Oil stayed elevated; Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it will pursue vessels that do not use approved routes, even outside the Strait of Hormuz.
The index closes match BigGo Finance's wrap (S&P 500 7,811.51, Nasdaq 27,366.17, Dow 51,654.95).
quote_evidence: Stocks climbed on Friday and ended the week on a high note after an AI-fueled drop on Thursday.

Tech shares rebounded after falling on Thursday following reports that OpenAI's annualized revenue hit $50 billion at the end of last month, lower than the $68 billion that had been previously reported.
Another report detailed on Friday that the company expects the figure to hit $70 billion by the end of the year, 40% more than September.
why_it_matters_hint: AI-heavy shares bounced back after a one-day scare over OpenAI's revenue, while households face weak sentiment and high prices.
event_date: 9 Oct 2026 (market close); the OpenAI revenue report was 8 Oct 2026
notes: Article gives $68 billion as the earlier OpenAI figure while Yahoo's other coverage and our 9 Oct edition say about $70 billion; summary avoids the earlier figure. Follow-up of the 9 Oct edition's OpenAI revenue item.
